Each has the cell pointer +0xe = 0xb1b8c8 and the index +0x26 = 0..5 in the image (no code writes item +0x26; the dispatchers 0x53cb41/0x53d2c1/0x53daae/0x53dc57 pass esi = the item, edx = the command, e.g. [0x82fd9c]), so the spec draws esi only from these six items (u32{=..}) and the item bytes stay as in the image except the flag byte +0x1f, varied here. Commands: 1 'and byte [esi+0x1f],0x7f' then, when the 16-byte cell [esi+0xe] = 0xb1b8c8 is not all zero ('or eax,[edi+4..0xc]; je'), 'repe cmpsd' of the cell with record [esi+0x26]*0x34 + 0xae6b68 and 'or byte [esi+0x1f],0x80' when equal; 2 copies that record into the cell ('movsd' x4) unless it is all zero, then calls 0x540be6 (or's the cell, walks the chain 0x848c6e through 0x53e4db/0x53e4e5, which tests/sets bits 0x20/0x40 of every chained item's +0x1f); 5 and 6 clear [0x82fd88]. The records 0xae6b68..0xae6c9f are the six 0x34-byte DirectInput device slots: 0x507740 fills their first 16 bytes with the null GUID 0x5f6280 (zero) and the EnumDevices callback 0x5078b0 ('cmp esi,6; jge' on the count [0xb1b3e0]) copies the device GUID (lpddi+8, 4 dwords) into slot [0xb1b3e0] and increments it - so the used slots are a filled prefix and the rest stay zero; 0x507650 copies slot 0 into the selected-device cell 0xb1b8c8. Drawn: the slot table 0xae6b68..0xae6c9f as 78 dwords filled up to n (prefix n in {0, 2, 13, 26, 39, 52, 65, 78}: 0..6 fully used slots, the rest zero, plus n = 2 where slot 0 has only its first two GUID dwords nonzero), nonzero dwords from {1 (6/7), 2}, so the indexed slot is a null GUID (command 2 skips the copy) or a used one; the cell 0xb1b8c8 (overriding cells_00540be6) all zero (no device selected: the 'je 0x540c8d' skip) or four nonzero dwords from the same values (prefix 0/4), so a used slot equals it in full in about a third of the cases ('or byte [esi+0x1f],0x80') and otherwise differs at dword 0..3 of the 'repe cmpsd'. The slot dwords +0x10..+0x33 (device name, +0x30 flags) are not read here. Any 128-bit value is valid: the GUIDs are only or'ed, compared and copied. Item flag bytes +0x1f of all eight chained items: any byte (and/or/test only). [0x82fd88] is only stored. Values are synthetic.
